Open source · tables, keys and owning services

Ops AI data model

Every table Ops AI keeps, grouped by the service that owns it, with its keys, its links and whether it is in code today. It is the companion to the Ops AI architecture page, whose service map and database sections it expands.

Ops AI is pre-release. Status labels describe the code at the date in the footer; planned tables and their columns are proposals.

built in code and a migration today planned designed, no code yet; dashed in the diagrams moving in code today, moving to another service; blue in the diagrams retiring in code today, removed when its replacement lands; listed in the tables only

How to read the diagrams

Notation

  • PKprimary key, FKkey of another table, UKunique.
  • ||--o{ one to many; ||--o| one to at most one; |o--o{ optional parent.
  • Each box shows the key columns and the columns that explain the table; the full columns are in each service's migrations.

Columns every table has

  • tenant_id on every table, which the store layer adds to every query.
  • team_id on every team-owned record, pointing at the team in identity.
  • Both are left out of the diagrams to save space.

Links across services

  • Each service owns its tables and reads only its own.
  • A link to another service's record is a stored key value, checked by that service's API.
  • Foreign key constraints exist only inside one service.
Why one section per serviceEach service owns its tables, so grouping by owner shows which service a change lands in, and answers the question a risk review asks of every table: which component can read this data.

1 Identity and teams

Owned by platform-service partial

Tenants, the people in them, the teams they belong to and the role each person holds in each team. API keys belong to a team. Every other table in Ops AI carries the tenant_id and, for team-owned records, the team_id defined here.

WhyAccess is granted per team, so the team is the unit every other service checks. Keeping identity in one service, the only one that issues tokens, means a change to who may do what happens in one place and every service sees it on the next token.
TableHoldsStatus
tenantsAn organisation using the platform, with the email domains allowed to sign inbuilt
teamsA group that owns agents, workflows, tools and knowledgebuilt
usersA person in a tenantbuilt
membersA person's role in one team; also holds pending invites. An invitation to an email that already has an account is accepted only by that person, signed in as themselves; the check runs inside the same transaction as the acceptance, and the unique email per organisation refuses a second account made at the same momentbuilt
api_keysA team's key for system access, stored as a hash with read or write scopebuilt
sessionsA signed-in browser session and its refresh token hashbuilt
audit_entriesWho did what, to which record, with the request idbuilt

2 Agents and runs

Owned by agents-service partial

An agent is versioned; each version is what a publish review approved. Every use of an agent, from a chat message to a background job, is a run on a thread. A thread keeps the conversation, its events, its checkpoints and the lease that says which process is running it.

WhyEach run stores the settings it actually used (effective_settings), because callers may choose a model, temperature, tools or knowledge within the agent's limits. The agent version alone then no longer says what a run did, and the stored settings make every answer explainable. Overrides set on a thread apply to every run in it; a run may narrow them further.
TableHoldsStatus
registry_agents, registry_agent_versionsAn agent and its immutable versions. A version carries the limits a caller may override within, the on or off switch of each pinned guardrail and optional call caps per turn and per conversation. An empty per-turn model-call cap means 50, and an empty per-conversation cap means 200 model calls and a cost of 5.00built
registry_publish_requestsA request to publish a version, decided by a second person. Moves to the reviews packagemoving
registry_skills, registry_skill_versionsVersioned procedures an agent loads when a request matches. A skill records who created it, once, so the right to delete it does not pass to whoever saved a draft lastbuilt
registry_guardrails, registry_guardrail_versionsVersioned checks on the question and the answerbuilt
graph_threadsA conversation or job thread, with the overrides set for the thread. Its origin and owning team are planned ix_graph_threads_team_updated (tenant_id, team_id, updated_at) serves a team's thread list (0071, c-280).partial
chat_attachmentsA file attached to a chat message: who owns it, its type and size, and the text read from it, cappedbuilt
chat_searchA thread's title, agent, last reply and questions as plain columns, so search works on every supported databasebuilt
registry_widgets, registry_widget_versionsWidget templates an agent may show in chat, saved as versions and published through a review. The newest name is kept on the widget so a list searches and pages in the databasebuilt
widget_deploymentsA chat widget served to pages on other origins: the agent and published version it is pinned to, the exact origins allowed, a paused flag and the team its conversations belong to. Sessions are signed tokens that expire after 15 minutes and are not storedbuilt
graph_versionsThe compiled graph a thread runs onbuilt
thread_eventsThe event stream of a thread: messages, tool calls, approvals ix_thread_events_tenant_team_position (tenant_id, team_id, position) serves the team event poll; it replaced ix_thread_events_team_position, which led with the team id alone (0071, c-280).built
thread_inboxMessages that arrive while a run is busy, delivered in orderbuilt
thread_leasesWhich process runs the thread now, with a generation number that fences out a stopped processbuilt
thread_budgetsThe model-call, token and cost caps of a thread, checked against what it has spent. A chat conversation gets its caps from its agent when it starts. When they are spent the conversation pauses, and its owner continues or a team admin raises them. An answer names the pause it answers, so a screen showing an older pause is refusedbuilt
model_call_recordsEach model call a run made, for replay and costbuilt
ops_checkpoints, ops_checkpoint_writes, ops_checkpoint_fencesRun state after each step, so a run resumes from its last step after a crash. Gain run and step columns ix_ops_checkpoints_run (tenant_id, team_id, (metadata->>'run_id')) serves the delete by run (migration 0071, c-280); like these tables it is raw SQL with no metadata until the checkpointer's SQL Server rewrite (c-337), so the diagram and the golden DDL do not show it.built
agent_runsOne run of an agent: mode, status and reason, settings used, budget and usageplanned
agent_run_queueBackground runs waiting for a workerplanned
agent_jobsA goal, a trigger and a budget; the agent works over many turns and ends with a reportplanned
graph_runsThe current run record, replaced by agent_runsretiring

3 Workflows and steps

Owned by workflows engine (served by agents-service today) built

A workflow definition is immutable once published and identified by workflow, version and digest. A run walks it step by step; every step attempt is a row in the journal, and the work queue hands steps to workers.

WhyThe journal and the work queue are what let a workflow survive a crash without repeating a write: a restarted run reads which steps finished and reconciles each write by its key. Only the workflows engine writes these tables. Each journal row records the hash of the node pack that ran it, so every step can be traced to the exact code.
TableHoldsStatus
engine_definitionsWorkflow definitions by version. Each version has a stage: draft, live, paused or superseded. A draft goes live when its publish review is approved. archived_at and archived_by are set on every version of an archived workflow, which starts no run (migration 0070, c-274) ix_engine_definitions_live (tenant_id, workflow_id) WHERE stage = 'live', on PostgreSQL and SQL Server alike, serves service event listeners and the mailbox listener (0071, c-280).built
engine_runsOne run of a workflow version, with status and outcome. A run another run's step started has created_by = run:<parent id>, which is how a parent finds the runs it waits on. Indexes: ix_engine_runs_parent_status (tenant_id, created_by, status) finds a parent's unfinished runs, ix_engine_runs_team_created (tenant_id, team_id, created_at) and ix_engine_runs_team_status_created (tenant_id, team_id, status, created_at) serve the runs list (migrations 0065 and 0066; 0066 replaced ix_engine_runs_created_by) ix_engine_runs_workflow_created (tenant_id, workflow_id, created_at) serves the runs list filtered by one workflow (migration 0071, c-280).built
engine_stepsThe step journal: one row per node, iteration and attempt. Gains pack id, version, hash and an output referencebuilt
engine_workThe work queue, claimed by workers under a lease Indexes: ix_engine_work_due (status, build, available_at) and ix_engine_work_lease (status, build, lease_expires_at), one per branch of the claim: due queued work, and claimed work whose lease lapsed (0071, c-280).built
workflow_timersWaits and deadlines inside a workflow runplanned
installed_packsNode packs installed at deploy time from the allowlist, pinned by hashplanned
node_typesThe node types each pack provides, written at start-upplanned
task_typesA Human Task type: the screen a review step or POST /v1/tasks names by id. Seeded types have no team; a team's own type is edited by that team. Holds the newest version and the published version, and where a copy came from. Row level security by tenant (migration 0063)built
task_type_versionsEach saved version of a task type as a JSON record. A published version never changes, so a task keeps the screen it opened with (migration 0063)built
case_typesThe fields a case shows and their order, per tenant: a seeded type (owned by no team, copied to change) or a team's own, with its newest and newest published version (migration 0069, c-291)built
case_type_versionsEach saved version of a case type: its fields, each with a key, label and type (the extraction field types, file or link). A case pins the published version it opened with (migration 0069)built
task_assistsWhat task assist wrote for a typed task when its step paused, one row per review step (step_id = run:node:iteration). A second write for the same step is refused, so a task costs one model call (migration 0064)built
registry_workflows, registry_workflow_versions, registry_validationsThe first workflow registry, replaced by engine_definitionsretiring
deployments, channel_messages, channel_cursors, channel_filesThe first mailbox channel, replaced by trigger bindings. A deployment records the team that owns it, so only a builder or administrator of that team can create, pause or poll it; deployments made before this existed have no owner until an administrator sets oneretiring

Today these tables are migrated with agents-service; they move to the workflows engine's own migration chain.

4 Reviews, triggers and work items

Owned by reviews (ops_hitl) and triggers (ops_triggers) partial

Reviews and triggers serve agents and workflows alike. A review is opened by any producer and resumed by its key; a decision mints an approval for that exact input. A trigger binding starts an agent job or a workflow run from a schedule, a webhook, an email or a poll. A work item is one entry in the shared work list.

WhyThese tables belong to packages that neither agents nor workflows own, so a deployment with only one of them keeps reviews and triggers. reviews.resume_key and work_items.subject_id point at a run by its key, because the run lives in another service's tables.
TableHoldsStatus
reviewsOne open review: who produced it, how to resume it, the options and the approval policyplanned
review_decisionsEach decision on a review. Exists in agents-service today and moves, keyed to the reviewmoving
review_approvalsThe approval minted for an exact input. Moves, keyed to the reviewmoving
timersSLA timers that fire each outcome once. Moves with reviewsmoving
casesA case in agents-service. fields (JSON, nullable) keeps what an Open case or Add to case step read or worked out, by name (migration 0062); type_id and type_version name the case type version it was opened with (migration 0069)built
work_itemsOne entry in the shared work list for agents and workflowsplanned
trigger_bindingsWhat starts which agent job or workflow, with a daily capplanned
trigger_eventsEach arrival, with a dedupe key so a repeat starts nothing newplanned
poll_cursorsWhere a polling trigger last read up toplanned

5 Tools and the data gateway

Owned by tools-service built

A tool module is one business system, imported from an OpenAPI description or an MCP server. It has operations, versions, a security review and approvals, and the hosts it may reach. Every call through the gateway is logged and fenced.

WhyCredentials, limits and the call log sit with the gateway, the only process that calls business systems. Agent workers hold no credentials, and a risk review of tool access examines one service's tables.
TableHoldsStatus
tool_modulesA connected business systembuilt
module_operations, module_versionsIts operations and their versions, each with an approval policy. An operation imported from OpenAPI keeps the JSON Schema of its first success response, so a workflow step shows its output fields before it runsbuilt
security_reviews, module_approvalsThe security team's review and approvals before publishbuilt
module_egress_hosts, egress_hosts, egress_ranges, egress_auditThe hosts and address ranges a module may reach, and each check madebuilt
gateway_calls, gateway_fencesEvery call with its verified caller and outcome, the environment and connection it used, the route that took it (the API or MCP) and the name an MCP client gives itself, reconciled by key; fences reject stale approvalsbuilt
connections, connection_environments, connection_auditHow the platform signs in to one system, per test and production, its credentials bound to the system's address; secret parts are rows of tool_secretsbuilt
connection_tokens, oauth_statesEncrypted OAuth tokens, stored against the rotation they replaced, and sign-ins in progressbuilt
operation_mocksAn operation's mock answers in test, which a test call gets before anything is sentbuilt
tool_secrets, secret_auditEncrypted credentials and every read of them. Each secret also lists the teams whose modules may read it; none means every teambuilt
operation_rate_windowsRate and amount limits held in the database, so they apply across every gateway processbuilt

6 Models and the AI gateway

Owned by models-service partial

Aliases such as gpt-5.5 map to a provider connection and a model id. Gateway keys belong to an identity (an agent, a workflow, a person or a purpose), each with a budget and rotation. Every call is logged.

WhyProvider credentials and spend sit with one service, so changing a provider or capping a team's spend is a change in one place, and every model call is metered the same way.

model_aliasesVersioned aliases with prices and the data sensitivity each is cleared forbuilt
model_keysGateway keys per identity, with budget, rate limit and rotationbuilt
model_call_logMetadata for every call: alias, tokens, cost, latency, outcomebuilt

7 Knowledge and files

Owned by kb-service and files-service partial

A knowledge base groups sources; a source yields items, each item has versions, and each version is split into chunks that answers cite by page and section. Files hold document metadata; the bytes sit in object storage. The files service is built to its first slice plus storage settings: an admin chooses a local folder, S3 or Azure Blob for each kind of file, with a test before every save. The file list, with its search, filters and counts, and bulk delete are built. The retention and clean-up jobs, resumable large uploads, setting retention from the console and virus scanning (off for now) are planned.

WhyVersioned items let an answer cite the exact text it used, even after the source changes. Keeping file bytes in the enterprise's object store and only metadata in the database keeps the database small and lets retention and legal hold follow the storage the enterprise already governs.
TableHoldsStatus
kb_bases, kb_sources, kb_base_sourcesKnowledge bases and the sources each includes; a base keeps the id of the source its files read into fields go to (documents_source_id, kb 0009)built
kb_items, kb_item_versions, kb_chunksDocuments, their versions and the passages retrieval returnsbuilt
kb_changes, kb_runsWhat changed on each sync, and each sync runbuilt
kb_retired_basesThe id of a deleted knowledge base, so a search that names it skips it and an agent keeps its other basesbuilt
filesOne row per file: type, digest, purpose, scan result, sensitivity, retention class and storage location. The storage location is shown to admins of the file's team only. The file list searches name, uploader and digest, filters by upload date, purpose, scan result and sensitivity, and counts each view (quarantined, under legal hold, unused for 30 days, expiring within 30 days) and each filter value with grouped queries, so no page counts rows it did not loadbuilt
file_blobsOne row per digest in a team, so two uploads of the same bytes share one stored file, even when they finish togetherbuilt
file_versions, file_references, file_legal_holdsEach version is its own stored object; a reference blocks deletion; a legal hold keeps its history after releasebuilt
file_idempotencyThe key of an upload request, so a retried upload returns the first filebuilt
storage_settingsOne versioned document per organisation: where each kind of file is stored, its limits and retention class, and how long a download link lasts. A save names the version it was made from, so two admins cannot overwrite each otherbuilt
storage_credentialsA storage credential by name, sealed with AES-256-GCM and never shown again; the settings document refers to it by namebuilt
storage_settings_auditOne row for every settings save and every credential set or deletion, written with the change; a credential is named and never valuedbuilt

8 Documents

Owned by documents-service built

The documents service reads a file into checked fields, each tied to where it is printed. It never holds the bytes: it reads them through the files client and keeps the file's id and digest. A document type has immutable versions holding its fields, layout templates, checks across fields, date order and whether reads may show the model the page image. A read is an extraction; a person's correction keeps the original beside it and reports extraction.corrected through the outbox. Its columns, routes and sequences: documents design.

WhyA version that never changes lets a workflow pin what it reads with, and lets a test run say which version scored what. Keeping the layout per file digest means the same bytes are parsed once, however many times they are read.
TableHoldsStatus
documents_layoutsOne file's layout per digest and layout engine version: pages, blocks, table cells and words with boxesbuilt
extractionsEach read: the fields with their boxes, the path (template or model), image calls, measured tokens and, for a model read, its layout fingerprint for template offers. Unique on the idempotency keybuilt
extraction_correctionsA person's correction of one field, with the original value and confidence keptbuilt
document_types, document_type_versionsA team's document types and their immutable versions: fields with rules and key fields, templates, checks, date order, page imagesbuilt
document_type_samples, document_type_testsFiles with the values a version should read, and priced test runs against thembuilt
document_type_examplesWhat corrections teach a type: the field, the line its value was printed on and the corrected value, one per read and field, per team. Later reads are given the newest few; a field keeps its newest 10, and a deleted file's examples go with its reads. People see the line and value masked as their team masks personal databuilt
documents_outboxCorrection events written with the correction and relayed to agents-service; delivered and replaced rows are pruned after 7 daysbuilt
examplesConfirmed corrections as few-shot examples for the typeplanned, c-297

Databases

The platform connects to a SQL database the enterprise runs, usually a managed instance. Each service may use its own database or share a server. Development uses PostgreSQL in a local container; unit tests use SQLite.

DatabaseStatusTenant isolation
PostgreSQL 15 to 17runs todayTenant filter in the store layer, with row-level security as a second check. Today row-level security covers run, checkpoint, workflow, chat attachment, chat search, widget deployment and identity tables
Azure SQL, SQL Server 2022plannedTenant filter in the store layer, with a row-level security policy on from the first release
MySQL 8.0 and 8.4plannedTenant filter in the store layer
RuleWhat it means for the schema
Store operationsRepositories call a small set of operations (current time, claim one row, upsert, lock a row, tenant and system transactions), each rendered per database
JSON columnsJSONB on PostgreSQL, JSON on MySQL, NVARCHAR(MAX) with a JSON check on Azure SQL. Queries filter on columns; a JSON field that needs filtering becomes a column
KeysBounded text with a binary collation, so Msg-1 and msg-1 stay distinct. Keys built from outside text are indexed through a SHA-256 column
LeasesRow locks with a generation number, which work on all three databases
MigrationsOne portable baseline per service, with database-specific parts such as row-level security kept in one helper
Why three databases and a store-layer filterBanks run the database they already license, and adding a new engine to a bank's estate takes months of approval. Row-level security exists only on some engines, so the tenant filter that must hold everywhere lives in the store layer, and each database's own row-level checks stay on as a second line where they exist.
